run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T08:03:37Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy returned HTTP 500s for POST /api/checkout, which is visible in both its own error spans and its own access logs. The failures trace to the checkout Deployment: revision 2 of Deployment otel-demo/checkout was rolled out at 2026-11-17T08:12:15Z with KAFKA_ADDR changed from kafka:9092 (revision-1 ReplicaSet) to kafka:9999 (revision-2 ReplicaSet, same image). The kafka Service only exposes plaintext 9092 and controller 9093, and the Kafka broker itself listens/advertises 9092, so the new checkout container times out dialing 100.66.162.182:9999 (the kafka Service ClusterIP) and crash-loops with exit code 2 (container terminated reason Error at 08:15:53 and 08:19:20, restartCount 1, BackOff event). Checkout therefore serves almost no PlaceOrder traffic, frontend's grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and POST /api/checkout spans turn to STATUS_CODE_ERROR plus tcp.connect errors from ~08:14, and frontend-proxy's ingress/egress error rate climbs from ~0.01/s to ~1.0-1.1/s while its total span rate is flat. Kafka itself is healthy and reachable on 9092, so a Kafka outage is not the cause. The alert's stated start (08:03:37Z) precedes the observed checkout-related surge (~08:13-08:14Z); a small nonzero frontend-proxy error rate (0.004-0.02 spans/s) was already present from the first available sample at 07:53, which may explain an 'above 0' alert starting earlier, but the alert rule itself could not be read.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) were 0.0037-0.022 spans/s between 07:53 and 08:13, then rose to 0.215/s at 08:14, 0.507/s at 08:15 and about 1.0-1.13/s from 08:17 to 08:22, on span_name "ingress" and "router frontend egress"; the STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate stayed at about 9-10 spans/s over the same period, so the error share rose while total traffic did not.

Inside frontend, the failing operations are POST /api/checkout and its client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder: their STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate is 0 until 08:13, 0.096/s at 08:14 and 0.52-0.57/s from 08:17 to 08:23, and frontend tcp.connect spans start reporting STATUS_CODE_ERROR (0.033/s at 08:14, about 0.04-0.06/s thereafter), while GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and GET /api/data show no error spans.

The frontend-proxy pod's own access log records repeated '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' responses forwarded to the frontend upstream (for example at 08:20:08.152Z, 08:20:10.747Z, 08:20:41.042Z), confirming the proxy itself served the 500s counted by the alert.

Deployment otel-demo/checkout is at deployment revision 2, and its current pod template sets env KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout); the Deployment reports unavailableReplicas 1 and condition Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable) as of the query.

The two checkout ReplicaSets show the change: checkout-5dccddf8bb (revision 1, created 07:38:57Z) has KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, while checkout-849d65649b (revision 2, created 08:12:15Z) has KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999; both use the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout, and both init containers still probe 'nc -z -v -w30 kafka 9092'.

Kubernetes events for otel-demo record the rollout at 08:12:15Z: Deployment checkout scaled checkout-849d65649b up from 0 to 1 and checkout-5dccddf8bb down from 1 to 0, old pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9d9c8 was killed, new pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz was scheduled on i-07a344976fd03ed38 and its wait-for-kafka and checkout containers started, followed by a BackOff event for the checkout container.

Pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz (owner ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b) started at 08:12:15Z and its checkout container is not ready: restartCount 1, lastState terminated reason Error exitCode 2 finishedAt 08:15:53Z, current state terminated reason Error exitCode 2 finishedAt 08:19:20Z.

The checkout container log shows the failure directly: repeated 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout' and finally 'kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout' between 08:12:47Z and 08:20:36Z, after retries it logs 'starting to listen on tcp: "[::]:8080"', and the running instance logs '[PlaceOrder]' and 'payment went through' at 08:15:53Z.

The kafka Service in otel-demo has clusterIP 100.66.162.182 and exposes only ports plaintext 9092 and controller 9093; its Endpoints point at pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh (100.96.4.148) with only ports 9092 and 9093. No port 9999 exists on the Service or its Endpoints, matching the dial target in the checkout error.
The Kafka Deployment configures KAFKA_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093 and KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092, so the broker itself does not offer port 9999.

The kafka pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh is Running, its kafka container is ready with restartCount 0 (started 07:38:58Z), and other clients use the correct port: Deployment accounting and Deployment fraud-detection both set KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092.

checkout's own spans stop rather than report errors: HTTP POST, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, orders publish, oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge rates fall from about 1.5-1.9/s (08:00-08:13) to 0 by 08:15-08:16, and every returned checkout series carries STATUS_CODE_UNSET only.

Service-level error-span rates over 07:50-08:27 show frontend (peak about 2.3/s) and frontend-proxy (peak about 1.1/s) as the only services with the large surge; ad, fraud-detection and recommendation each show only intermittent 0.0037 spans/s both before and after 08:13, and accounting, payment and checkout show 0 error spans/s.

The fault is the KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 value in the revision-2 template of Deployment otel-demo/checkout: because the kafka Service has no 9999 port, checkout's Sarama producer cannot connect, the container exits with code 2 and crash-loops, checkout becomes unavailable for PlaceOrder, frontend returns 500 for POST /api/checkout, and frontend-proxy's error rate crosses the alert threshold.

A pre-existing low-level frontend-proxy error rate (0.0037-0.022 spans/s in the first samples, from 07:53, before the checkout rollout) may explain why an 'error rate above 0' alert was reported as starting at 08:03:37Z, ahead of the checkout-related surge; this cannot be confirmed because the RequestErrorRate rule could not be retrieved.

Kafka is not the failing dependency: the kafka pod is Running and ready with 0 restarts, the broker listens/advertises only 9092/9093, the checkout pod's wait-for-kafka init container successfully waited on 'nc -z kafka 9092' before the checkout container started, and accounting/fraud-detection use kafka:9092. The dial failure is to port 9999, which exists nowhere in the Kafka config or Service.
Payment was not failing for the one order checkout processed: the checkout container logged 'payment went through' at 08:15:53Z, and payment shows 0 error spans/s across the window.

Flagd fault-injection flags are not the cause of this failure: the flagd-config ConfigMap lists kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure and similar flags, but every one is ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off', and the observed failure path is a TCP timeout to port 9999 rather than a flag-declared fault.

A Kafka broker outage is rejected as the cause: the kafka pod is ready with 0 restarts, the broker advertises PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092, the Service/Endpoints expose 9092, and no Kafka-side error is observed; only checkout's new pod fails to connect, and it fails against a port the broker never exposes.

Correct the checkout workload configuration: set KAFKA_ADDR back to kafka:9092 in Deployment otel-demo/checkout (and in whatever source applied revision 2 at 08:12:15Z), then confirm the rollout produces a ready checkout pod, that checkout's 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999' lines stop, and that POST /api/checkout stops returning 500 at frontend-proxy.

Add a pre-rollout check that every host:port in a workload's env resolves to a declared Service port (checkout referenced kafka:9999 while the kafka Service only declares 9092 and 9093), since the pod-level init container probing 9092 masked the bad application port.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no rules, so the rule expression, threshold and the 08:03:37Z alert start cannot be verified against the observed error-rate curve that surges from ~08:13-08:14Z.
Prometheus samples for frontend-proxy and frontend span metrics begin only at 07:53-08:05 in the returned series, so no baseline exists for the earlier part of the 24h authorized window.

Jaeger in this environment only holds traces up to 08:01:04Z (5000-trace retention); traces_search for frontend at 08:16-08:17Z and traces_search_by_tags with error=true returned nothing, so no span-level error detail is available for the 08:14+ failures.
The frontend pod's own logs returned no lines for 08:00-08:27Z and 08:14-08:27Z, so the frontend-side exception text behind the 500 responses is unknown.
Change history integration is not available, so what or who applied Deployment checkout revision 2 at 08:12:15Z (and why KAFKA_ADDR became kafka:9999) cannot be established.

The exact image digests of the revision-1 and revision-2 checkout ReplicaSets were not compared (only the identical image string ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout), so the claim that this was a configuration-only change rests on the identical image tag and differing env value.
next_steps: Inspect the source of truth (Helm values / GitOps commit for release otel-demo, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2) to find where KAFKA_ADDR was set to kafka:9999 and revert it to kafka:9092.

After correcting and rolling out checkout, watch checkout pod readiness, checkout log lines for kafka:9092 connectivity, frontend POST /api/checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate and frontend-proxy ingress/router-frontend-egress error rate to confirm recovery.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate alert rule definition to confirm the threshold and evaluation window, and reconcile the reported 08:03:37Z start with the observed 08:13-08:14Z error surge.
Verify whether the bad KAFKA_ADDR value also exists outside this cluster's checkout Deployment (for example in the chart values or another environment) to prevent recurrence.
